tagline: Up Francis Thornton's valley, under the bare top of Old Rag.
intro: From the county seat at Madison, Route 231 follows Blue Ridge Turnpike north and crosses the Robinson River near Banco, where it turns onto F.T. Valley Road. The F.T. is Francis Thornton, the same man who gave Thornton Gap its name.

The road runs up his valley through the foothills of the Blue Ridge, past Etlan directly east of Old Rag Mountain, and through Peola Mills into Rappahannock County, ending at US 522 near Sperryville. The designated byway begins farther south at Gordonsville, crossing the Southwest Mountains and the Rapidan to reach Madison; the line drawn here starts at Madison.

moments.title: Madison
moments.text: A county seat of 205 people in 2020, where Route 231 shares Main Street with the old line of US 29 before heading north on Blue Ridge Turnpike.

moments.title: Old Rag Mountain
moments.text: Unlike most of the Blue Ridge it has a bare rocky summit of granite about a billion years old, and the most common way up starts at Nethers, off Route 231.

moments.title: Sperryville
moments.text: Francis Thornton Jr. began selling lots for his little town in 1820, and by 1880 it had a woolen mill, seven distillers, four general stores and one saloon.
